source.title: The Retrieval Bottleneck: Scaling Laws for Reinforcement Learning in RAG
source.authors: Shu Zhou; Jinman Leng; Yufei Song; Xin Wang; Tao Fan; Hao Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether scaling-law behavior transfers to RAG reinforcement learning. It reports sigmoid rather than power-law scaling for that setting and shows that fitted curves and parameters vary with the task and configuration.
record.gate_note: The paper studies RL training steps and task performance in RAG, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy, parameter/token scaling, or parameter-token compute-optimal allocation. Only its own RAG-RL scaling fits, setup-dependent scaling results, and related RAG-RL extrapolation and document-count results are recorded. Comparisons of methods that do not report scaling outcomes are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study fits sigmoid curves of task accuracy (EM or accuracy) against RL fine-tuning steps for one fixed 8B RAG model. It does not measure held-out loss against parameters, tokens or pretraining compute. It does not fit or compare a power-law alternative, and it assumes the sigmoid form from prior RL-scaling work. Bounded task-accuracy curves over RL steps are a related but different construct from the power-law loss laws in V1–V7. The parameter variation across tasks, retrievers and algorithms comes from different training setups, not from different fitting choices on the same data, so it does not bear on V7. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only as motivation.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that RAG-RL follows sigmoid scaling and that retrieval quality, not RL compute, bounds the ceiling. Design choices mainly modulate efficiency. The 3.1% error at 4× compute comes from a single NQ extrapolation (8K→32K steps).
record.recipe_differences: This is a study of RL compute scaling for RAG task performance, not pretraining loss scaling in parameters, tokens, or total compute. It fits sigmoid curves and varies retrieval and RL configurations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported fitted scaling parameters and ceilings vary by benchmark, corpus size, retriever quality, and RL algorithm/objective. The study also reports compute-dependent optimal document count.

fits_no_version.finding: RAG-RL task accuracy over RL steps (1K–64K) follows S-shaped curves on HotpotQA, NQ and FEVER with LLaMA-3-8B. The sigmoid form was assumed from prior RL work; no power-law fit was compared.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RL fine-tuning performance in RAG follows a sigmoidal curve in RL compute, bounded by retrieval quality.

fits_no_version.finding: Fitted ceiling A tracks retriever Recall@5 (r=0.97). Corpus size, RL algorithm and objective shift A, B and Cmid.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In RAG-RL, retrieval quality sets the performance ceiling, while RL design choices mainly modulate compute efficiency.

fits_no_version.finding: For NQ, the preferred number of retrieved documents increases with RL compute: the paper reports k*=5 at 8K steps and k*=10 at 32K steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In RAG-RL, compute-optimal retrieval document count can increase with training compute.

fits_no_version.finding: Sigmoid fits on partial NQ data extrapolate EM with 0.4–3.1% error over 2–4× compute extensions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A fitted sigmoid can predict RAG-RL task performance over short and moderate compute extensions in the tested setup.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The scaling experiments use a single 8B generator and focus on three knowledge-intensive benchmarks, primarily extractive QA and fact verification. The authors state that frontier-scale models and generative or long-form tasks may behave differently. Some numerical uncertainty is reported, but not for every fitted scaling parameter in the tables.
record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges' label for V5 and 'supports' label for V7 are dropped. The study never tests a power law against its sigmoid. It measures bounded task accuracy over RL steps for a single 8B model, not loss over parameters, tokens or pretraining compute. Its parameter variation reflects different training setups, not fitting choices on the same data. Rows r7, r9 and r14 repeat the same baseline NQ configuration (A=51.8).

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameter count, tokens, or compute is not measured.
The study extrapolates RAG-RL task performance using its sigmoid fits, not power-law predictions of held-out loss on runs orders of magnitude larger.
No compute-optimal split between model parameters and training tokens is measured.
Architecture depth, width, or other architecture variations at fixed parameter count are not tested.
Tests only RAG reinforcement learning on knowledge-intensive QA and fact verification; does not test other modalities, repeated data, general fine-tuning, or transfer.
The study measures task performance over RAG-RL compute, not downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss or model scale.

Shows configuration- and task-dependent RAG-RL sigmoid fit parameters, but does not compare competing fitting methods, parameter-counting rules, or published pretraining-law estimates; does not test parameter-token compute-optimal allocations.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Fit sigmoid scaling curves to EM versus RL training steps with fixed retrieval configuration.
rows.measure: Fitted sigmoid parameters for EM versus RL compute
rows.value: R0=45.0; A=67.2; B=1.42; Cmid=8.3K training steps
rows.note: The authors describe the observed scaling curves as S-shaped, rather than a power law.
rows.check: Sigmoid fit of EM against RL steps for one model, with no power-law fit or loss measure. It cannot show whether a power law holds, so 'reversed' for V5 is not supported. Differences in fit parameters across tasks are not V7 fit-dependence.
